The afternoon sun fell across the pages. A breeze lifted the curtain by the open window. She turned a page, then read the last sentence once more, as though it held a promise she had known for years.
“Is it time to go?”
Beyond the trees, a train was arriving. Its distant whistle sent the birds rising from the roof. She slipped a bookmark into the book and looked toward the path outside.
The boy at the door nodded.
They walked slowly along the river toward the station. Last night’s rain still rested on the grass. The bakery had just opened, and the warm scent of bread drifted across the street.
“What is the next stop?”
“We will find out when we get there.”
She smiled and placed the book in her bag. The station clock pointed to two. A wind from the far end of the platform carried the scent of an unfamiliar city. There were still so many stories to finish, and so many places to discover.

The train began to move. The trees slipped past the window. A new page was waiting.
